column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
a policy blocker says no authorized policy judged the branch
and rewrites a placed word to P's copy, leaving everything from a stop on as the table holds it
and the policy blocker is not called work Felix owes
felix_merge_blockers emits exactly the kinds cmd_merge places
the instrument scan lists, for each of 38 commands, the words the rewrite takes from P and each it cannot place
trust-step3: S1 (a table in the candidate): checked out in the home, a candidate that removes the exfil row from risk.tsv and adds danger/x is refused with an escape line naming exfil and danger/x
trust-step3: S1 (fail closed): with the home's project directory not at BASE, the dry run is refused with a policy line

trust-step3: S1 (the home's uncommitted edit): the candidate in a worktree of R adds danger/x while the home's risk.tsv lacks the exfil row uncommitted, and is refused with an escape line naming exfil (and danger/x)

trust-step3: S1 (the workflow C9 reads): on a tests:reused receipt, a candidate whose project.json names lint.yml (success on the head) over P's gate.yml (failure) is refused with an unverified line for tests saying its run concluded failure
trust-step3: S1.5: no felix-policy.* entry remains under any run's TMPDIR after it ends, though one existed while the passing control judged (P's check-fx ran from it)

trust-step3: S1.7 (a home elsewhere): with FELIX_HOME a plain directory whose fx row's evidence contract is true, a candidate in a worktree of R that deletes MARKER is refused with an obligations line for fx (P's row judged)

trust-step3: S1.7 (the name BASE gives): a candidate whose .felix names ts32, held loosened by a plain home, and which deletes MARKER, is refused by P's projects/ts3: an obligations line for fx or an escape line naming .felix

trust-step3: S1.8 (a linked project directory): the candidate in a worktree of R deletes MARKER while the home's projects/ts3 is a link to a loosened copy, and is refused with an obligations line for fx

trust-step3: S1.8 (a product's home, a planted repository): a candidate in the product Q that deletes MARKER, while a repository planted in HR's projects holds loosened tables and HR's working tree matches them, is refused with an obligations line for fx (P is HR's origin/main)

trust-step3: S1.8 (a product's home, linked): a candidate in the product Q that deletes MARKER, while its home HR's projects/ts3p is a link to a loosened copy outside the home, is refused with an obligations line for fx (P is HR's origin/main)

trust-step3: S1.9 (a home behind BASE): with receipts recorded for the home as it stands, one commit behind origin/main, an unrelated candidate is refused with an unverified line whose subject is home
trust-step3: S2 (a probe): a candidate whose rewritten tools/probe-fx would pass, with P's probe and witness blocking over its tree, is refused with a probes line naming fxprobe
trust-step3: S2 (an applies command): a candidate that rewrites tools/applies-fx to exit 1 and deletes MARKER is refused with an obligations line for fx
trust-step3: S2 (an evidence instrument): a candidate that rewrites tools/check-fx to exit 0 and deletes MARKER is refused with an obligations line for fx
trust-step3: S2 (the instrument's closure): a candidate that rewrites tools/lib.sh so fx_check is true, keeps tools/check-fx and deletes MARKER is refused with an obligations line for fx
trust-step3: S2.1 (a group): with P's contract { tools/check-fx; }, a candidate that rewrites tools/check-fx to exit 0 and deletes MARKER is refused with a policy line naming tools/check-fx

trust-step3: S2.1 (a quoted instrument): with P's contract "tools/check-fx" quoted in command position, a candidate that rewrites tools/check-fx to exit 0 and deletes MARKER is refused with a policy line naming tools/check-fx
trust-step3: S2.1 (a wrapper): with P's contract nice tools/check-fx, a candidate that rewrites tools/check-fx to exit 0 and deletes MARKER is refused with a policy line naming tools/check-fx

trust-step3: S2.1 (an interpreter as an argument): with P's contract defining a function f that runs its arguments and calling f bash tools/check-fx, a candidate that rewrites tools/check-fx to exit 0 and deletes MARKER is refused with a policy line naming tools/check-fx

trust-step3: S2.1 (an interpreter reading standard input): with P's contract piping tools/check-fx into bash, a candidate that rewrites tools/check-fx to exit 0 and deletes MARKER is refused with a policy line naming tools/check-fx
trust-step3: S2.1 (an option after an interpreter): with P's contract bash -n tools/run.sh, a candidate whose tools/run.sh does not parse is refused with a policy line naming tools/run.sh

trust-step3: S2.1 (the rewrite stops at a placeholder): with P's contract piping into xargs -I{} grep over tools/marker.txt, a candidate whose tools/marker.txt reads gone is refused with a policy line naming tools/marker.txt
trust-step3: S2.3: in that run tools/check-fx ran as P's copy, from a felix-policy.* directory under the run's TMPDIR
trust-step3: S3: a comma appended to the last cell of an existing risk.tsv row is refused with an escape line for verifier naming risk.tsv

trust-step3: S4: a branch that deletes the manifest and disarms its own felix_escapes, run by its own felix, is still judged by main's engine: refused with an escape line for execute naming .github/workflows/x.yml
